release_note: Batch 5 adds six hidden optional flowering/spikelet character groups with direct source-page citations to Diggs et al. (1999). Evidence only ranks positively, never excludes or promotes a specimen ID. Setaria bristles, Arundo lemma hairs and Phragmites rachilla hairs are separated.

characters.label: Leaf blade shape
characters.hint: Look at a fresh, expanded blade. V-folded and inward-rolled leaves are different. Drying or drought may change the apparent shape.

characters.label: Leaf width
characters.hint: Measure a fresh blade near its widest point. Ranges are approximate and can overlap; flatten curled leaves when practical.

characters.label: Leaf tip
characters.hint: Examine a mature intact tip, not one torn by mowing or grazing.

characters.label: Blade edge
characters.hint: Observe under a hand lens. Some grass edges can cut skin; don't drag fingers across them.

characters.label: Leaf midrib
characters.hint: Look along the center of the blade, separate from its edge.

characters.label: Veins, ribs & grooves
characters.hint: Look at both sides of a fresh blade with a hand lens. Parallel veins are common to grasses; a white center vein, raised single keel, paired pale grooves and many lengthwise ribs are different structures.

options.label: Two pale grooves beside the midrib

characters.label: Leaf blade hairs
characters.hint: Use a hand lens if needed. Check whether hairs occur mostly at the base or across the blade. Collar and sheath hairs are separate.

characters.label: Leaf base / sheath
characters.hint: Look where a blade joins its sheath. Ears (auricles) are separate from ligules.

characters.label: Ligule height
characters.hint: Open the blade–sheath junction to measure the true ligule, not adjacent collar hairs.

characters.label: Ligule edge
characters.hint: Find the inner papery flap or hair fringe. A ragged edge differs from fine hairs growing off its margin.

characters.label: Leaf sheath opening
characters.hint: Check a fresh leaf. Closed sheaths sometimes split as they dry.

characters.label: Leaf sheath shape and feel
characters.hint: Examine the sheath surrounding the stem, not the exposed blade.

characters.label: How the stem grows
characters.hint: Follow a stem, not just a drooping leaf. Knee-bent stems bend at a real joint; decumbent stems lie low but turn upright at the end. All extra answers are optional.

characters.label: Surface runners and rooting
characters.hint: A stolon is a separate creeping horizontal stem with nodes. A low flowering stem that roots at one joint is not necessarily a stolon.

characters.label: Underground stems
characters.hint: A rhizome has real stem nodes and scale leaves. Don't call ordinary roots or a short crown a rhizome, and do not dig plants where collection is restricted.

characters.label: Stem base and crown
characters.hint: Look at an attached plant base. Hard, knotty perennial crowns differ from long creeping runners; large cane stems are a separate clue.

characters.label: Other stem clues
characters.hint: Uncommon features can help with look-alikes, but verify them on the same grass as the other observations.

characters.label: Node hairs and gland rings
characters.hint: Examine an actual joint on the stem. Hairs at the ligule or leaf collar are different from node hairs. Some species vary by plant and season.

options.label: Hairs on a surface runner's joints

characters.label: Florets in one spikelet
characters.hint: Check one mature spikelet with a hand lens. Several tiny florets can sit inside one spikelet, not on separate seedhead branches.

characters.label: How spikelets sit
characters.hint: Follow the actual little spikelets on a flowering branch: a stalked/stalkless pair differs from separate rows or one-sided branches.

options.label: On one side of a branch

characters.label: Outer glumes
characters.hint: Look at the two outer spikelet scales, not the leaf sheath. A hand lens helps with small veins.

characters.label: Lemma surface
characters.hint: Check a floral scale itself for hairs, wrinkles, reddish marks or shininess. A hairy flower stalk is not a hairy lemma.

characters.label: Awns on the lemma
characters.hint: A true awn grows from a floral scale. Setaria's surrounding bristles are different structures. Some species vary.

characters.label: Bristles and floral hairs
characters.hint: Check where hairs attach: under the spikelet, on the rachilla, on the lemma, or on the stalk of a reduced partner.
